## Question 3

"Turn the 11 areas options into yes/no columns and cluster the students (hierarchical clustering or k-modes), or reduce with PCA/MCA and plot. What I'd look for: whether a "modern ML" group (deep learning, images, NLP, deployment) separates from a "classical stats" group (inference, time series, visualization). Follow-up: check whether the clusters differ in language preference or in industry vs. lab."

Can we identify distinct groups of students based on their data science interests, and how do these groups differ in their programming preferences and project goals?"

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

background <- read_csv('../data/background-clean.csv', show_col_types = FALSE)
interest <- read_csv('../data/interest-clean.csv', show_col_types = FALSE)
# Split the interests by comma and count them
interest_counts <- interest %>%
  separate_rows(areas, sep = ",") %>%
  mutate(areas = str_trim(areas)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(areas), areas != "") %>%
  count(areas, sort = TRUE)

#removes "generally" b/c the "," was messing it up 
#note if it was important - please go over 
interest_counts <- interest %>%
  separate_rows(areas, sep = ",") %>%
  mutate(areas = str_remove(areas, ",?\\s*generally")) %>%
  mutate(areas = str_trim(areas)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(areas), areas != "") %>%
  count(areas, sort = TRUE)

# Graph the interests
ggplot(interest_counts, aes(x = reorder(areas, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "pink", color = "black") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Topic Interests Among Students",
    x = "Topic Intrests",
    y = "Number of Students"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
#I redid this so can someone please run it to make sure it works on their end. It was working when I ran the code but when I tried to render it it stopped. I finally got it to work but can someone else please take a look (and delete this comment after)

#What areas do students normally chose together? 
interest_long <- interest %>%
  mutate(student = row_number()) %>%
  separate_rows(areas, sep = ",") %>%
  mutate(areas = str_trim(areas)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(areas), areas != "", areas != "generally") %>%
  distinct(student, areas)

interest_binary <- interest_long %>%
  mutate(selected = 1) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = areas,
    values_from = selected,
    values_fill = 0
  )

interest_matrix <- interest_binary %>%
  select(-student)

set.seed(123)
clusters <- kmeans(interest_matrix, centers = 3)
interest_binary$cluster <- clusters$cluster

cluster_summary <- interest_binary %>%
  select(-student) %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean), .groups = "drop")

pca <- prcomp(interest_matrix)
cluster_plot <- as.data.frame(pca$x[, 1:2])
cluster_plot$cluster <- as.factor(clusters$cluster)

ggplot(cluster_plot, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Student Clusters Based on Data Science Interests",
    x = "Principal Component 1",
    y = "Principal Component 2",
    color = "Cluster"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
#Cluster 1 Red: Students who commonly selected deep learning and image analysis.
#Cluster 2 Green: Students who commonly selected databases, deep learning, and model deployment
#Cluster 3 Blue: Students who commonly selected statistics, visualization, and data acquisition
```

```{r}
#What do the clusters mean 
cluster_graph <- cluster_summary %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -cluster,
    names_to = "Interest",
    values_to = "Percentage"
  )
ggplot(cluster_graph, aes(x = factor(cluster), y = Interest,
                          fill = Percentage)) +
  geom_tile(color = "black") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Percentage * 100), "%")),
            size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Data Science Interests by Cluster",
    x = "Cluster",
    y = "Data Science Interest",
    fill = "Proportion"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#What language does every cluster prefer 
interest_binary$cluster <- clusters$cluster
interest_language <- interest %>%
  mutate(student = row_number()) %>%
  left_join(
    interest_binary %>% select(student, cluster),
    by = "student"
  )
ggplot(interest_language,
       aes(x = factor(cluster), fill = language)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", color = "black") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Programming Language Preference by Cluster",
    x = "Cluster",
    y = "Percentage of Students",
    fill = "Language"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
